title: East St. Louis Baby, Boyd's Bounce and the Wasco label
summary: The interviewer asks about songs on Wasco; Longhair says they were put together overnight and cannot recall who owned the label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah, well that always happens. Do you remember the song of East St. Louis Baby?
And the song of Boyd's Bounce? No, those are just putting those together overnight. It's just, imagination.

Because it's listed here in a label called Wasco. Wasco. Wasco. Do you remember that label? Mm-hmm. Is that what it appeared on? I've never seen the record. Yeah. I've never seen that record. Boyd's Bounce. What label? It's a black label.
Who owned it? I don't recall who had that label.

Like I said, if I knew that these were the questions you were going to ask, I'd have brought my briefcase. It would have been more simple to ask because I have all the listings of the questions that you're asking, but it's hard to remember right off hand, you know, without looking in a book. Mm-hmm. But you don't remember who owned Wasco or?
